Workshop · Námskeið · 5–8 October 2026

Advanced acoustic workshop
Marine and Freshwater Research Institute, Hafnarfjörður


Four days on calibration, ADCP operation, acoustic scrutiny with Korona and LSSS, biomass estimation in R, AI for data processing and MFRI acoustic data in the cloud, with a field trip to Teledyne Gavia and a final day of project work.

title: Software setup
text:
Please install LSSS, Python and R on your laptop before the workshop starts on Monday 5 October. Allow about 45 minutes. If something fails, bring your laptop on Monday morning and we will sort it out together.
On an MFRI laptop you may need administrator rights for the Windows installers. If so, contact MFRI IT.

title: Software setup
text:
LSSS
LSSS (Large Scale Survey System) is free software from Marec. The download also includes KORONA, which we use on Wednesday. These instructions are for LSSS 3.3.0 (September 2026). The download is about 130 MB.

WindowsmacOS



Go to https://marec.no/downloads.htm and download lsss-3.3.0-20260902-0905.exe.
Run the installer. If Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”, click More info → Run anyway.
Start LSSS from the Start menu.



The Mac version of LSSS is built for Intel processors. On a Mac with an Apple chip (M1–M5), it runs through Apple’s Rosetta 2 translation layer.

Check your chip. Open the Apple menu → About This Mac. If Chip says Apple M…, install Rosetta once in Terminal:
softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license
Go to https://marec.no/downloads.htm and download lsss-3.3.0-20260902-0905-macos.zip.
Double-click the zip in Downloads. It contains a second zip, lsss-3.3.0-macos.zip. Double-click that one too.
Move the resulting lsss-3.3.0 folder into your home folder.
LSSS is not signed by Apple, so macOS will block it. Allow it to run with this Terminal command:
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/lsss-3.3.0
Start LSSS by double-clicking lsss-3.3.0/lsss/LSSS.command. KORONA’s launchers are in lsss-3.3.0/korona/.




Memory. By default, LSSS uses 2/3 of your computer’s memory, up to 30 GB. To use less, set the environment variable LSSS_MAX_MEMORY_MB, e.g. 4096.
Check: LSSS opens and shows its main window.

title: Software setup
text:
Python
We use Miniforge, a small, free installer that gets packages from the open conda-forge channel. You don’t need an Anaconda licence. If you already have Python through Anaconda or Miniconda, skip step 1 and run step 2 in that installation.

WindowsmacOS



Download Miniforge3-Windows-x86_64.exe from https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest and run it. Choose Just me and keep the default options.
Open Miniforge Prompt from the Start menu and create the workshop environment:
conda create -n acoustics -c conda-forge echopype jupyterlab matplotlib
Type y when asked.




Open Terminal and run the following. It picks the right version for Intel or Apple-chip Macs automatically.
curl -L -O "https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-$(uname)-$(uname -m).sh"
bash Miniforge3-$(uname)-$(uname -m).sh
Press Enter to read the licence, type yes to accept, and keep the default location. When asked whether to initialise conda, answer yes. Then close Terminal and open it again.
Create the workshop environment:
conda create -n acoustics -c conda-forge echopype jupyterlab matplotlib
Type y when asked.




Check: in Miniforge Prompt (Windows) or Terminal (macOS), run
conda activate acoustics
python -c "import echopype; print(echopype.__version__)"
If this prints a version number, Python is ready. To start Jupyter during the workshop, run conda activate acoustics and then jupyter lab.

title: Software setup
text:
R
We use R together with RStudio, a program for writing and running R code, in the biomass session on Wednesday. Install R first, then RStudio.

WindowsmacOS



Go to https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/, download the latest R installer (Download R-4.x.x for Windows) and run it with the default options.
Go to https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/, download RStudio Desktop for Windows and install it.




Go to https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/ and download the latest R installer for your chip: arm64 for Apple M… Macs, x86_64 for Intel Macs. Open the .pkg and follow the steps.
Go to https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/, download RStudio Desktop for macOS, open the .dmg and drag RStudio into Applications.




Open RStudio and install the workshop packages by typing this in the Console:
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "sf", "rmarkdown"))
Check: run library(tidyverse) in the Console. If no error appears, R is ready.
